Command: The New Commandment: Love One Another
Summary: The command Jesus gave on the night before the cross: love one another as he has loved — a love measured by his own self-giving.
Commandment: Love one another just as Christ has loved you; let this love mark you as his disciples.
Application: The commandment is called new not because love was new, but because its measure is new: as I have loved you, even to laying down life for friends.
Purpose: Measured by Christ's own self-giving love (John 13:34); the mark of discipleship (John 13:35).
Function: The commandment is called new not because love was new, but because its measure is new. This comes from the New Testament, not from Sinai, so the old threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was love measured by Christ's own self-giving — as I have loved you, even to laying down life for friends. The evil it addressed was love that stops short of sacrifice. It restrained that evil by the mark itself: by this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
